verdicts.title: Endless self-avoiding walks
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We introduce a self-avoiding walk model for which end-effects are completely eliminated. We enumerate the number of these walks for various lattices in dimensions two and three, and use these enumerations to study the properties of this model. We find that endless self-avoiding walks have the same connective constant as self-avoiding walks, and the same Flory exponent $ν$. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns 'endless self-avoiding walks' on 2D/3D lattices, studying connective constants, Flory exponent ν, and critical exponent γ=1 — purely a statistical-mechanics SAW paper. It says nothing about ACC^0[2] circuits, MOD_3, or gate-incidence multigraphs, so it neither supports nor refutes the conjecture.

verdicts.title: Self-avoiding quantum walks: realisations in subspaces and limit theorems
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: While completely self-avoiding quantum walks have the distinct property of leading to a trivial unidirectional transport of a quantum state, an interesting and non-trivial dynamics can be constructed by restricting the self-avoidance to a subspace of the complete Hilbert space. Here, we present a comprehensive study of three two-dimensional quantum walks, which are self-avoiding in coin space, in position space and in both, coin and position space. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns quantum walks on two-dimensional lattices with self-avoidance restricted to coin/position subspaces of Hilbert space, not Hammersley connective-constant enumeration on gate-incidence multigraphs of ACC^0[2] circuits. It shares the 'self-avoiding walk' vocabulary but does not interact with circuit lower bounds or MOD_3.
